findings.title: Width-fitting truncation exceeded the ADR-009 24-scalar hard limit (fixed and verified)
findings.acceptance_criterion: 2 (drawing engine / typography / truncation) and ADR-009 'Text limits and truncation'
findings.original_defect: BadgeLayoutEngine.FitToWidth tried retained prefixes up to scalarCount-1 without capping against the policy scalar limit, so a 24-scalar over-wide label could be emitted as 25 or 26 scalars (including '...').
findings.fix_verified: FitToWidth (src/ArrTags/Rendering/BadgeLayoutEngine.cs:238-274) now computes maximumRetained = policy.MaximumScalarValues - CountScalarValues(policy.Ellipsis), returns null (omission) when maximumRetained < 1, and bounds the loop to Math.Min(scalarCount - 1, maximumRetained). Every candidate is therefore retained + ellipsisScalarCount <= MaximumScalarValues, and the early-return path returns already-normalized text that is <= the limit. The same bounded FitToWidth is used by both the technical rail and the status pill.
independent_reproduction: Real bundled DejaVu Sans Bold 2.37, reviewer's original 16xU+0057 + 8xU+1671 (U+1671 = 56px at 28px, full label 944px > maxTextWidth 928, width 1000): final pill text is now scalarCount=24 ('16 W + 5 U+1671 + ...'), width 809 <= 928. Before the fix this same case produced 26 scalars.
Pure synthetic over-wide case ('a'*22 + 'WW', W=100/other=41/'.'=2, width 1000): final text is now 24 scalars, not the previous 25.
Status-pill path with the same over-wide label is also bounded to 24 scalars.
Within-limit label '1080p' is returned unchanged (no ellipsis, no regression).
Under heavy width pressure the label shortens further (11 scalars in the probe; the regression test asserts < 24).
A label that cannot produce a visible label at all is omitted (empty layout).

New regression tests WidthFittingKeepsFinalTextWithinTheAdr009ScalarLimit and WidthFittingStillShortensFurtherUnderMoreWidthPressure cover the 24-scalar bound and further shortening and would have failed against the pre-fix loop.

findings.title: Present-but-unparseable ICC profile is not rejected fail-closed (deferred to 4.11, unchanged)
findings.description: ADR-010 requires an invalid or unsupported embedded profile to fail closed. SkiaBadgeRenderer relies on Skia's decode into an sRGB destination; an independent probe with a correctly-CRC'd but garbage iCCP chunk still decoded successfully as sRGB rather than failing.
findings.assessment: Confirmed real divergence, but the malformed/unsupported-profile rejection assertions are explicitly scoped to the ADR-010 PNG-contract tests (task 4.11), so it is acceptable to defer for 4.9 as directed. The orchestrator must ensure 4.11 (or a follow-up implementation task) actually delivers fail-closed profile rejection, because 4.11 is described as a test task. Not a 4.9 blocker.

findings.title: RenderAsync throws ArgumentNullException for a null request (left unchanged, as directed)
findings.description: The null-request guard is conventional, documented in IRenderer, and covered by SkiaBadgeRendererDecisionTests.NullRequestIsRejected. Content-level invalid input is correctly returned as a bounded Failed/PassThrough result. Not a blocker.

findings.title: RenderRequest did not snapshot the BadgeDefinition list (fixed and verified behavior-preserving)
findings.fix_verified: RenderRequest now copies the supplied definitions into a new List<BadgeDefinition> and exposes a ReadOnlyCollection (definitions.AsReadOnly()). The observable read behavior, ordering, count validation, and null-entry behavior are unchanged; no test compares BadgeDefinitions by reference, and the full suite passes. This closes the minor mutability gap noted in the first review.
